findings.text: The price functions read pair balances, not pair reserves
Token deposits are valued at a pool price the caller can move
The daily mint converts BNB to tokens at a pool price the caller can move
The batch mint reads one pool price that the caller can move
The token deposit path skips the whitelist check
An inflated principal lets a seller skip the profit tax

An upline that rejects BNB blocks deposits from its downline: Code smells: `safeTransferETH` to up to 20 uplines inside the loop; one revert fails the whole deposit; only an owner `setBlackLists` call removes the block — An upline contract that reverts on receipt makes `_addPool` fail for every downline deposit. The attacker gains no tokens, and the owner can

The deposit swap and liquidity add accept any output: Code smells: `swapExactETHForTokens(0, ...)`; `addLiquidityETH(..., 0, 0, ...)`; `deadline = block.timestamp` — An attacker who trades before and after a deposit takes part of the swapped BNB. We did not measure the profit after swap fees.

Blacklisted uplines still collect speed credit: Code smells: the upline loop adds to `userSpeedBNBCount` with no `!blackList[superAccount]` check; `_addPool` has this check — A blacklisted upline collects speed credit and uses it after the owner removes the blacklist entry. We did not show a gain above `canTakeBNBTotal`.

Any BNB that arrives during the sell swap goes to the seller: Code smells: `getBNBAmount` is the `address(this).balance` difference around the swap; `receive()` accepts BNB from any sender — BNB that reaches the core between the two balance reads counts as the seller's proceeds. We did not find a token hook that sends BNB there.

The LP burn after a sell raises the price for the next seller: Code smells: `IToken(Token_Address).burnLP(sellTokenAmount * sellBurnTokenRatio / DENOMINATOR)` runs after the user payout — A holder who sells through the core and then sells on the DEX from a second account gets more BNB. We did not verify `burnLP` or the profit after the profit tax.

Tokens moved to a high-principal account escape the profit tax: Code smells: the profit tax compares sales with the seller's own `userAddBNBCount`, but the sold tokens can come from any account — A reward holder moves tokens to an account with a high principal and no sales, and that account sells them with no profit tax. The sell swap accepts any output: Code smells: `swapExactTokensForETH(sellTokenAmount, 0, ...)`; the user cannot set a minimum output — An attacker who trades before and after a user sell keeps part of the BNB of that user.

The sell branch sends BNB back before it reads the token balance: Code smells: `safeTransferETH(account, BNBValue)` runs before `balanceOf(account)` and `_sellToken`; the account gets control first — The account can change its token balance or allowance before the sale. We did not confirm a re-entry path through the out-of-scope token.
